comment: The escalation examples cover scope, capacity, stakeholder conflict, security and continuity. Clinically consequential events are not named. A serious identity, terminology, interoperability or workflow defect could therefore continue to be handled as an operational technology incident when it also requires patient-safety review.

public.text: The escalation examples cover scope, capacity, stakeholder conflict, security and continuity. Clinically consequential events are not named. A serious identity, terminology, interoperability or workflow defect could therefore continue to be handled as an operational technology incident when it also requires patient-safety review.
public.suggestedRevision: Add explicit escalation triggers for actual or suspected patient-safety events; clinically significant performance degradation; unsafe identity, data, terminology or decision-support behaviour; and change-induced workflow hazards. Define time-bound escalation to the relevant clinical-governance or patient-safety authority, including regulatory reporting where required, and criteria for service restriction, rollback or suspension.
